paragraphs: Crossover characters are a genre of their own: a figure from one world dressed for another, so that the armour becomes a jacket and the sword becomes something with a power cell. This is a white haired swordsman rebuilt for a neon lit city rather than a forest road.

The character holds 164,436 polygons and 87,748 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. The library also carries a T pose build, a walking pose and a rigged version, and it is built to CheckMate specification.
At $139 it suits game characters, concept and fan art, animation and previsualisation, science fiction illustration and editorial work. On sale since 2024.

The dachshund was bred to go down a badger hole, which explains everything about the shape. A dapple coat is the mottled pattern that comes from a single gene, and a dog lying on its back is the pose owners photograph most and modellers supply least.

The animal holds 31,119 polygons and 30,992 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the repeated coat pattern, and is supplied in the reclining pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $139 it suits pet and lifestyle visualisation, veterinary and pet product marketing, interior renders, advertising, animation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A launcher in the deployed configuration is a different vehicle from one on the road: outriggers down, the platform levelled, the erector raised. Everything that makes it mobile is now working to make it stable, because accuracy depends on the ground more than on the missile.
The model holds 1,053,225 polygons and 1,160,849 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, supplied deployed for combat. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $139 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film and game environments, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Female cranial anatomy differs from male in ways that matter for surgery and for sculpture alike: the brow, the jaw angle and the proportions of the face. Modelling it specifically rather than adapting a male head is the only way those differences survive into the render.
The model holds 179,330 polygons and 179,988 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $139 it suits medical and dental education, surgical and aesthetic visualisation, anatomy reference for artists, forensic reconstruction and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A floating dock solves the tide. It rises and falls with the water, and the hinged ramp to shore takes up the difference, which is why marinas and lake moorings look the way they do rather than being built on piles.
The scene holds 92,852 polygons and 97,077 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the dock together with a boat and the access ramp. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $139 it suits waterfront and marina visualisation, architectural and landscape scenes, tourism and leisure imagery, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The frog is the animal biology classes dissect, and generations of students learned where a heart sits by looking at one. A modelled version does the same teaching without the specimen, and can be rotated, exploded and repeated in a way a real dissection cannot.
The model holds 51,219 polygons and 51,308 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the internal organ structure. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $139 it suits biology and veterinary education, museum and exhibition work, scientific illustration, animation and editorial material. On sale since 2022.

An empty machine is a specific kind of unsettling. A military robot with no pilot and no operator is either waiting or abandoned, and the viewer has to decide which, which is why the pose matters more here than any weapon fitted to it.
The model is listed at 747 polygons over 388,240 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, finished in dark green, and carries StemCell certification.
At $139 it suits science fiction film and animation, game characters and environments, concept art, technology illustration and editorial work. On sale since 2024.

Magirus has been building fire appliances since the ladder was made of wood, and the name still carries the trade. On an Iveco chassis, the FF160 is the workhorse version of that: a pump, lockers full of kit and a crew cab, sized for European streets rather than American ones.
The model holds 413,278 polygons and 466,832 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification. A rigged build is offered separately.
At $139 it suits emergency services visualisation, safety and training material, urban and architectural scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2022.

The T900 Legend was built as a farewell: a limited run of a long nosed conventional, trimmed the way owner drivers had been ordering them for decades. Australia took most of them, and the shape became a fixture on road train routes.

The model holds 269,674 polygons and 302,780 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 22 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $139 it suits transport and logistics visualisation, automotive and haulage marketing, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The standalone fast food restaurant is a building type in its own right: a drive through lane wrapped around the kitchen, parking on three sides, and a sign visible from the road at speed. The architecture is entirely a consequence of the car.
The model holds 278,346 polygons and 301,174 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the building and its surroundings. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $139 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, retail and commercial property presentation, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The MTVR was built around independent suspension, which is unusual for a military truck of this size and is precisely why it goes where others cannot. Every wheel moves on its own, so the load stays level across ground that would rack a conventional chassis.
The vehicle holds 456,084 polygons and 478,371 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 14 maps all at 4096x4096, and carries StemCell certification.
At $139 it suits military logistics visualisation, defence presentation, documentary and film, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

A quadriga is four horses abreast pulling a chariot, and it has crowned triumphal architecture since antiquity. The arrangement is deliberately impractical as a vehicle and perfect as a sculpture, because four horses seen from the front fill a roofline the way nothing else does.
The model holds 137,947 polygons and 138,793 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $139 it suits architectural and historical visualisation, museum and exhibition work, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The ice cream van is a delivery truck with a serving hatch cut into it, and that improvisation is the whole charm. A 1949 Chevrolet body in white gives the period exactly: post war, chrome trimmed, and built when a van still looked like a car with a box on the back.

The model holds 126,735 polygons and 129,863 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the wheels and hatch can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits period film and television, advertising and food marketing, street and architectural scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The same suit design served two very different programmes. On the Moon it had to survive dust, sunlight and a two hundred degree swing in temperature; on Skylab it mostly had to work inside a station, and the differences between those versions are in the fittings rather than the shape.
The model is light at 20,330 polygons and 20,827 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $129 it suits space history and documentary work, museum and education material, film and television, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
